text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Wednesday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- Riga's city council decided to repair the Victory Monument without allocating additional budget resources. The mounument to Soviet soldeiers who fought in the Second World War was damaged by a bomb on June 6.

- NATO invited Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic to begin membership talks. Latvian diplomatic sources said that the Baltic countries have been placed in the same boat as Romania and Slovenia and will make the next wave of expansion.
- The chief of Latvian state police, Aldis Lieljuksis, has breached the anti-corruption law by being a member of the board of the security firm Poligons.
- The government has approved the bill on courts of arbitration.
- UN Secretary- General Kofi Atta Annan has accepted an invitation from President Guntis Ulmanis to visit Latvia.
- Russia's leading private airline company Transaero plans to acquire 12 new aircrafts and Parekss bank will likely participate in a consortium of four to six banks to raise the funds.

- Estonian computer manufacturer MicroLink plans to start producing hardware in Latvia this year. It will invest about $100,000 in Latvia. MicroLink has the biggest market share in the Baltic countries with 15.1 percent of the total market.
